# Account vectors: <label> <nonce> <balance> <storageRoot> <codeHash> <rlp>
# nonce and balance are decimal; the rest is hex without 0x.
#
# TWO CLAIMS, AND THEY ARE SEPARATE. A header that names only the encoder
# reads as full provenance and is not: this file asserted one and was read as
# asserting both, which is how six constructed rows sat under a corpus- label.
#
# THE OCTETS were produced by the executable specification's own
# encode_account -- not by this project and not by a client:
#   ethereum/execution-specs, release tests@v20.0.1
#   (87aba1a38a476b31f819a2390eb481527e6dc683, 2026-07-15)
#
# THE FIELD VALUES come from two different published corpora, and the label
# says which rows they cover:
#   ethereum/tests   c67e485ff8b5be9abc8ad15345ec21aa22e290d9 (2025-06-04)
#   the same release's fixture set, blockchain_tests and state_tests
#
#   corpus-*     a real published account from fixture pre-state. Every one
#                was located in one of the two corpora above by exact
#                (nonce, balance, codeHash).
#
#   authored-*   CONSTRUCTED HERE, and published nowhere. The table walks
#                nonce and balance BYTE-WIDTHS, because RLP encodes a
#                quantity in its minimal form and each width is a different
#                encoding shape -- and no corpus supplies an account at some
#                of those widths. A chain account does not carry nonce
#                2^64-1. The value is authored; only the label was ever
#                wrong. Named for the bucket it fills: kind, nonce width,
#                balance width.
#
# Only accounts whose storage is EMPTY are taken, so every row's storage root
# is the empty root. That restriction is now liftable -- the trie exists and
# its two-level root is certified -- and lifting it would make an L1 fixture
# depend on L2-derived values, which is a decision rather than an extension.
#
# The empty-trie root and the empty-code hash are derived at generation from
# first principles -- keccak of the RLP of the empty string, and keccak of no
# bytes -- never recalled.
#
# scripts/gen-account-vectors.py regenerates the corpus- rows. It does NOT
# reproduce this file row for row: this table predates it and did not record
# which account filled each bucket, so a regeneration picks a different, also
# published, account for some buckets. The generator's own pick rule is
# deterministic; this file's was never recorded.
